sense: the sharp end of a sword or blade

terms.gloss: a sharp point or edge, especially the point of a sword; also the sword itself

phrases.latin: stat ferrī aciēs mūcrōne coruscō stricta, parāta necī
phrases.english: a line of steel stands drawn, its points flashing, ready to kill

phrases.latin: nisi mūcrōnēs etiam nostrōrum mīlitum tremere voltis dubitantīs utrum in cīve an in hoste fīgantur
phrases.english: unless you want even the sword-points of our soldiers to waver, unsure whether they are being driven into a citizen or an enemy

phrases.latin: gallō canente spēs redit, aegrīs salūs refunditur, mūcrō latrōnis conditur, lāpsīs fidēs revertitur
phrases.english: at cockcrow hope returns, health flows back into the sick, the robber’s blade is put away, faith comes back to the fallen

long-u.html: The vowel stands before cr, so a heavy syllable in verse does not prove it long. De Vaan 391 heads the entry mūcrō, and the Latinitas loci collections write it so.

sources: Lewis & Short: mucro
